Measurement and Vectors: Scalar
A quantity with magnitude only, such as speed or mass
Vector
A quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as velocity
Resultant vector
The single vector equivalent to two or more combined vectors
Vector component
The projection of a vector along the x or y axis
Significant figures
The digits in a measurement carrying real precision
SI units
The international standard system: metre, kilogram, second
Dimensional analysis
Checking or converting units to verify an equation makes sense
Precision
How closely repeated measurements agree with each other
Accuracy
How close a measurement is to the true value
Order of magnitude
The approximate size of a quantity expressed as a power of ten
Kinematics in One Dimension: Change in position, a vector from start to finish
Total path length travelled, a scalar
Rate of change of displacement, including direction
Rate of change of distance, without direction
Velocity at a single moment in time
Total displacement divided by total time
Motion under gravity alone, with acceleration about 9.8 metres per second squared
A graph whose slope gives velocity
A graph whose slope gives acceleration and whose area gives displacement
Kinematics in Two Dimensions: Projectile motion
Motion under gravity with independent horizontal and vertical components
Range of a projectile
The horizontal distance travelled before landing
Trajectory
The curved path followed by a projectile
Independence of motion
Horizontal and vertical motion do not affect each other
Launch angle
The angle above horizontal at which a projectile is fired
Relative velocity
Velocity measured with respect to a particular frame of reference
Frame of reference
The viewpoint from which motion is measured
Horizontal velocity in projectile motion
Stays constant when air resistance is ignored
Vertical velocity at the peak
Momentarily zero at the highest point of the path
Time of flight
How long a projectile stays in the air
Newton's Laws of Motion: Newton's first law
An object keeps its state of motion unless a net force acts on it
Inertia
An object's resistance to a change in its motion, measured by mass
Newton's second law
Net force equals mass times acceleration
Newton's third law
For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction
Net force
The vector sum of all forces acting on an object
Free-body diagram
A sketch showing every force acting on a single object
Normal force
The support force a surface exerts perpendicular to itself
Weight
The force of gravity on a mass, equal to mg
Tension
The pulling force transmitted through a rope or cable
Equilibrium
The state where the net force is zero and acceleration is zero
Mass versus weight
Mass is the amount of matter; weight is the gravitational force on it
Action-reaction pair
Two forces acting on different objects, which is why they never cancel
Friction and Circular Motion: Friction
A force opposing motion between surfaces in contact
Static friction
Friction preventing an object from starting to move
Kinetic friction
Friction acting on an object already sliding
Coefficient of friction
A number describing how rough a pair of surfaces is
Air resistance
A drag force opposing motion through air
Terminal velocity
The constant speed reached when drag balances weight
Centripetal force
The inward force keeping an object moving in a circle
Centripetal acceleration
Acceleration directed toward the centre of a circular path
Period of revolution
The time for one complete trip around a circle
Tangential velocity
The instantaneous velocity along the circle, perpendicular to the radius
Work, Energy, and Power: Work
Force times displacement in the direction of the force
Joule
The SI unit of work and energy
Kinetic energy
Energy of motion, one half mass times velocity squared
Potential energy
Stored energy due to position or configuration
Gravitational potential energy
Energy from height, equal to mgh
Elastic potential energy
Energy stored in a stretched or compressed spring
Conservation of energy
Total energy in a closed system stays constant
Mechanical energy
The sum of kinetic and potential energy
Power
The rate at which work is done, measured in watts
Efficiency
Useful output energy as a percentage of input energy
Hooke's law
Spring force is proportional to how far it is stretched
Work-energy theorem
Net work on an object equals its change in kinetic energy
Momentum and Collisions: Momentum
Mass times velocity, a vector quantity
Impulse
Force times the time it acts, equal to the change in momentum
Conservation of momentum
Total momentum stays constant when no external force acts
Elastic collision
A collision conserving both momentum and kinetic energy
Inelastic collision
A collision conserving momentum but losing kinetic energy
Perfectly inelastic collision
A collision where the objects stick together afterward
Recoil
Backward motion of one object when it pushes another forward
Impulse-momentum theorem
Impulse applied equals the resulting change in momentum
Centre of mass
The average position of the mass of a system
Crumple zone
A design that extends collision time to reduce the force experienced
Rotational Motion: Rate of change of angular position, in radians per second
Rate of change of angular velocity
A twisting force, equal to force times lever arm
The perpendicular distance from the axis to the line of force
Rotational resistance to change, depending on mass distribution
Moment of inertia times angular velocity
Angular momentum stays constant without external torque
The angle where arc length equals the radius
The state where net torque is zero
Gravitation: Universal gravitation
Every mass attracts every other mass
Gravitational constant
The proportionality constant G in Newton's law of gravitation
Inverse square law
Gravitational force falls off with the square of the distance
Orbital velocity
The speed needed to maintain a stable orbit
Escape velocity
The speed needed to break free of a body's gravity
Kepler's first law
Planets orbit in ellipses with the sun at one focus
Kepler's second law
A planet sweeps equal areas in equal times
Kepler's third law
Orbital period squared is proportional to orbital radius cubed
Weightlessness
The sensation of free fall, not the absence of gravity
Gravitational field
The region where a mass exerts gravitational force
Simple Harmonic Motion: Oscillation where restoring force is proportional to displacement
The time for one complete oscillation
The number of oscillations per second, in hertz
The force pulling an oscillator back toward equilibrium
A mass swinging on a string, whose period depends on length and gravity
The rest point where net force on the oscillator is zero
The gradual loss of amplitude due to friction or resistance
Large amplitude growth when driven at the natural frequency
The frequency at which a system oscillates on its own
Waves and Sound: A disturbance transferring energy without transferring matter
A wave whose oscillation is perpendicular to its travel direction
A wave whose oscillation is parallel to its travel direction, like sound
The distance between successive identical points on a wave
The combining of two waves into a larger or smaller resultant
Waves adding to produce a larger amplitude
Waves cancelling to produce a smaller amplitude
A pattern of fixed nodes and antinodes from interfering waves
The shift in observed frequency caused by relative motion
The logarithmic unit of sound intensity
Light and Optics: The full range of light, from radio waves to gamma rays
The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection
The bending of light as it passes between materials
How much a material slows light relative to a vacuum
The relationship predicting how much light bends at a boundary
Light reflecting entirely inside a medium past a critical angle
A converging lens, thicker at the centre
A diverging lens, thinner at the centre
The distance from a lens or mirror to its focal point
The spreading of light as it passes an edge or slit
Restricting light waves to a single plane of vibration
Electrostatics: Electric charge
A property of matter that can be positive or negative
Coulomb's law
Electric force is proportional to charges and inversely to distance squared
Conductor
A material allowing charge to move freely
Insulator
A material resisting the movement of charge
Electric field
The region where a charge experiences electric force
Charging by friction
Transferring charge by rubbing two materials together
Charging by induction
Rearranging charge in an object without direct contact
Grounding
Providing a path for excess charge to leave an object
Electric potential
Electric potential energy per unit charge, measured in volts
Conservation of charge
Charge is never created or destroyed, only transferred
Electric Circuits: The rate of flow of charge, measured in amperes
The electrical potential difference driving current
Opposition to current flow, measured in ohms
Components on a single path, sharing the same current
Components on separate branches, sharing the same voltage
Rate of energy use, equal to voltage times current
An unintended low-resistance path causing dangerous current
A safety device interrupting excessive current
A component storing charge and energy in an electric field
Current entering a junction equals current leaving it
The single resistance that could replace a combination
Magnetism: Magnetic field
The region where a magnetic force acts
Magnetic pole
The north or south end of a magnet, where the field is strongest
Electromagnet
A magnet created by current flowing through a coil
Right-hand rule
A method for finding the direction of a magnetic force or field
Electromagnetic induction
Generating voltage by changing the magnetic field through a loop
Faraday's law
Induced voltage depends on how fast magnetic flux changes
Lenz's law
An induced current opposes the change that produced it
Generator
A device converting mechanical energy into electrical energy
Motor
A device converting electrical energy into mechanical motion
Transformer
A device changing voltage using two coils and induction
Modern Physics: Photoelectric effect
Light ejecting electrons from a metal, evidence that light is quantised
Photon
A single quantum, or particle, of light
Wave-particle duality
Light and matter each show both wave and particle behaviour
Quantum
The smallest discrete amount of a physical quantity
Special relativity
Einstein's theory that time and space depend on relative motion
Time dilation
Moving clocks run slow relative to a stationary observer
Mass-energy equivalence
Energy equals mass times the speed of light squared
Nuclear fission
Splitting a heavy nucleus, releasing energy
Nuclear fusion
Combining light nuclei, the process powering stars
Half-life
The time for half a radioactive sample to decay
Antimatter
Particles with the same mass but opposite charge to ordinary matter
Uncertainty principle
Position and momentum cannot both be known with perfect precision
